subject: Mathematics: Analysis & Approaches

parts.label: b
parts.html: Using rectangles under and over y=x^2, prove n^3/3<S_2(n)<n^3/3+n^2+n for n>=1.

parts.label: c
parts.html: Use S_2(n)-S_2(n-1)=n^2 to motivate a cubic polynomial S_2(n)=an^3+bn^2+cn+d and determine a,b,c,d.

parts.label: d
parts.html: Conjecture and prove by induction a formula for S_3(n).

parts.label: e
parts.html: Compare the leading terms with integral_0^n x^k dx and state a general conjecture.

solparts.label: b
solparts.html: Monotonicity of x^2 gives lower and upper rectangle sums; integrating produces the stated bounds after rearrangement.

solparts.label: c
solparts.html: Substitute the cubic into S2(n)-S2(n-1)=n^2 and compare coefficients, then use S2(0)=0: S2=n(n+1)(2n+1)/6.

solparts.label: d
solparts.html:
The data suggest
S3=[n(n+1)/2]^2. Verify n=1. Assuming true for n, add (n+1)^3 and factor to obtain
[(n+1)(n+2)/2]^2.

solparts.label: e
solparts.html:
The leading term is n^(k+1)/(k+1), matching the integral; conjecture
S_k(n)~n^(k+1)/(k+1).

parts.label: d
parts.html: Show the gradient of the circle at (x,y) is -(x-5)/(y-1), and find tangents at the two points.

parts.label: e
parts.html: The line y=mx passes through the origin. Determine the values of m for which it is tangent to the circle.

parts.label: f
parts.html: Find the area of the smaller sector between the two radii from part (c).

questions.title: Investigation: complex loci and geometry
solution:
The locus is the circle centre (5,1), radius 3, parametrized as stated. At t=pi/3 the point is
(13/2,1+3sqrt3/2); at t=-pi/2 it is (5,-2). Implicit differentiation of (x-5)^2+(y-1)^2=9 gives y'=-(x-5)/(y-1). Use point-slope form at each point. For y=mx, tangency requires
|5m-1|/sqrt(m^2+1)=3. Hence 8m^2-5m-4=0 and m=(5+/-3sqrt17)/16. The smaller angle is 5pi/6, so sector area=(1/2)(3^2)(5pi/6)=15pi/4.

instructions: Answer every question. Give reasons for conclusions, label graphs and diagrams, and include units where appropriate. A formula booklet may be used.
